This year can be said to be the year of super apps. OpenAI recently launched its own super app, but immediately admitted it was "a bit of a mess." Now Microsoft's CEO has also confirmed that a Copilot super app will be launched in the near future.

Microsoft Copilot "super app" will integrate Cowork, chat, coding and other features

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that combines Copilot's chat, coding, and agent capabilities into one. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on Wednesday's earnings call that the app will launch within this year and span "consumer and commercial experiences." Nadella said: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat to Cowork to Autopilot. This quarter we will integrate these Copilot experiences—including coding—into a single super app... This is an important step, and I look forward to sharing more details soon."

OpenAI's launch of its own "super app" has already turned into a disaster, but that clearly hasn't stopped other companies from following the super app strategy.

Perhaps Microsoft can build a one-stop app that stumbles less than OpenAI's.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella recently hinted that the company is shifting from an app-centric model to an agent-centric one. The AI era is still nascent, and the trends and best practices for building AI interfaces are still evolving.

As for Apple, it has not been seen moving toward a super app, and continues to launch standalone, specialized new apps. Whether that strategy will change in the future is worth watching.

What are your thoughts on the recent "super app" craze? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
